Verdict

No confirmed malicious supply-chain compromise indicators. Overall risk: **info**.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators found.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • In the reviewed material, there is no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, setup.py execution, install-time scripts, or clearly malicious PEP 517 build hooks.
  • Several src/bioversions/sources/*.py files contain if __name__ == "__main__": ...print(), but this only runs when those files are executed directly and is not evidence of install-time or interpreter-startup execution.
  • README/PKG-INFO examples such as bioversions web and bioversions get are normal user-triggered CLI usage.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • **Credential harvesting:** Not observed. Mentions of .pypirc, PyPI tokens, and keyring appear in maintainer documentation in README/PKG-INFO and are not paired with file discovery, token collection, or broad environment-variable harvesting code.
  • **Archive staging / exfiltration:** Not observed. .zip URLs, gzip, and requests.get/post appear in the context of querying public biological database versions or constructing public download URLs. There is no evidence of harvested-file compression, temp staging, external uploads, webhooks, or C2-style exfiltration.
  • **Persistence:** No evidence of systemd units, cron jobs, launch agents, shell profile modification, or background persistence loops.
  • **Kubernetes/CI/cloud lateral movement:** No evidence of kubeconfig access, cloud metadata access, Docker socket use, GitHub Actions token theft, or workflow injection.
  • **Obfuscation/loader:** The long base64 string in README/PKG-INFO appears to be an image/png;base64 badge/logo, not an executable loader. re.compile usage is for parsing version strings. No eval/exec/compile, marshal/pickle loader, encrypted payload, or download-and-execute behavior was identified.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Based on the provided manifest/corpus, there is no evidence of hidden payloads, unexplained native binaries, typosquatting, suspicious .dist-info tampering, or sudden malicious dependency insertion.
  • The many external URLs appear consistent with the package’s stated purpose of checking biological database versions or with documentation/badge links.

Additional Verification Needed

  • The input corpus is selective and does not include the full text of all 83 files. Full review of pyproject.toml, src/bioversions/__init__.py, cli.py, __main__.py, and any sdist-vs-wheel differences would provide higher confidence.
  • From the evidence provided, there is no basis to classify this package as a malicious supply-chain attack.
